decisions.quote: We replicated the prior finding of a main effect of higher alcohol consumption among individuals reporting earlier drinking onset. Age at drinking onset accounted for about 5% of the variation in PYDD, and this association was mostly attributable to overlapping genetic influences. Evidence for an interaction between onset age and SLE was generally weak, possibly because of lower power and other methodological differences from Dawson and colleagues’ study. However, there was some evidence consistent with an interaction of higher PYDD among early drinking men who experienced independent SLE and early drinking women with dependent SLE.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly frame their findings as partly replicating and partly not: they replicated the main effect of early drinking onset on past-year alcohol consumption, whereas the primary targeted interaction between total stressful life events (totSLE) and drinking onset was not statistically significant in either sex (explained as 'differences in results' from Dawson et al., 2007), with significant interactions emerging only in specific sex-by-event-dependence subgroups (independent SLE in early-onset men and dependent SLE in early-onset women, but not the reverse). Under the codebook, when the main effect replicates and the targeted interaction fails overall or holds only in partial subgroup analyses, the outcome is 'mixed'.
